subtitle: Social-Bi-Co Unrelationing

sections.heading: PART ONE · DIVIDING
sections.why: The part describes how philosophy splits one coupling into two opposed positions, which is an account of a fixing in the file's own subject.

sections.heading: 1.1 Core, bi-moral co-agency and philosophical dilemma
sections.why: It defines a philosophical position and a philosophical dilemma as one coupling fixed on two sides, which is the file's subject.

sections.heading: 1.2 A position, a dilemma, and the six run one-way
sections.why: It explains how a position fixes one side and how a dilemma splits into two traditions, an account of a fixing in philosophy.

sections.heading: 1.3 Dividing method, one requirement worn four ways
sections.why: It examines philosophy's analytic method and its four requirements as the source of perennial problems, an observing of the field's own fixing.

sections.heading: PART TWO · RE-COUPLING
sections.why: The part sets out re-coupling as the resolving of philosophical dilemmas and gives the six-step form each new seam follows.

sections.heading: 2.1 Re-coupling, and philosophy's own reaches
sections.why: It describes re-coupling as resolving a dilemma and reads philosophy's own landmark thinkers as earlier re-couplings that re-landed.

sections.heading: 2.2 Form each seam-explaining takes
sections.why: It gives the six-step method each philosophical dilemma is worked through, a method open to new dilemmas as a self works them.

sections.heading: PART THREE · SEAMING
sections.why: The part works thirty-seven named philosophical dilemmas one by one, each a fixing resolved.

sections.heading: 3.1 Being and becoming
sections.why: It resolves the metaphysical dilemma of permanence and flux as one self-equilibrating form.

sections.heading: 3.2 Mind and body
sections.why: It resolves the mind-body problem as one self-bounding surface with two sides.

sections.heading: 3.3 Free will and determinism
sections.why: It resolves the free will dilemma as a self's own binary taking; a closing paragraph on aligning built systems is a side surfacing and not the section's subject.

sections.heading: 3.4 Subject and object
sections.why: It resolves the knower-and-known dilemma of epistemology as one coupling of observer and observed.

sections.heading: 3.5 The one and the many
sections.why: It resolves the metaphysical dilemma of unity and plurality as one form surfacing many times.

sections.heading: 3.6 Is and ought
sections.why: It resolves the fact-value gap as one moral taking and works it through a proverb and a cake shared between two selves.

sections.heading: 3.7 The flowing now and the block
sections.why: It resolves the philosophy-of-time dilemma of presentism and the block as each self keeping its own time.

sections.heading: 3.8 Meaning and use
sections.why: It resolves the rule-following problem as meaning made with each use and stored nowhere.

sections.heading: 3.9 Cause and effect
sections.why: It resolves the problem of causation as a two-way coupling a still observer fixes to one side.

sections.heading: 3.10 Vagueness, and the demand for a landing line
sections.why: It resolves the sorites problem as a between with a parity and no line.

sections.heading: 3.11 Foundation and coherence
sections.why: It resolves the epistemic regress as a ground each coupling makes.

sections.heading: 3.12 Induction, and the un-repeating
sections.why: It resolves the problem of induction as a going on that seats its own next.

sections.heading: 3.13 The whole and its parts
sections.why: It resolves the reduction and emergence dilemma as an aggregate arising among couplings, using economics' aggregation results as material.

sections.heading: 3.14 Other minds
sections.why: It resolves the problem of other minds as an interior reached only by coupling between two selves.

sections.heading: 3.15 Identity and change
sections.why: It resolves the persistence problem as a going on that stores nothing between its beats.

sections.heading: 3.16 Finite and infinite
sections.why: It resolves the philosophical dilemma of the actual and potential infinite as a gathering making its own bound.

sections.heading: 3.17 Self-reference
sections.why: It resolves the liar paradox as a sharing with nothing coming back.

sections.heading: 3.18 Consistency and completeness
sections.why: It resolves the philosophy-of-mathematics question raised by incompleteness as a derivation reaching to its own system's bound.

sections.heading: 3.19 Skepticism and the world
sections.why: It resolves external-world skepticism as an experience arising with its own coupling.

sections.heading: 3.20 Discovering numbers and making numbers
sections.why: It resolves the platonism and formalism dispute as a mathematical practice that goes on the same under either view.

sections.heading: 3.21 Theory and observation
sections.why: It resolves underdetermination and theory-ladenness in philosophy of science as choosing that lives with couplings.

sections.heading: 3.22 Structure and agency
sections.why: Its dilemma is posed by social theory about persons and social arrangements as two levels of a society, a subject of social scales rather than of philosophy.
sections.home: Exhibit_SEVEN_Natural_Societies_v392.md (Natural Societies: Co-Recursioning Up and Down Social Scales)

sections.heading: 3.23 Learning and knowing
sections.why: It resolves the paradox of inquiry and explains discovering a new concept as recognising it while observing it.

sections.heading: 3.24 Part and whole in reading
sections.why: It resolves the hermeneutic circle as a changing and changing back a reader rides.

sections.heading: 3.25 Aboutness
sections.why: It resolves the problem of intentionality and symbol grounding as content each coupling makes.

sections.heading: 3.26 Universals and particulars
sections.why: It resolves the realism and nominalism dispute about kinds as classifying that makes its kinds.

sections.heading: 3.27 Knowing and its conditions
sections.why: It resolves the Gettier problem as knowing being a coupling that no list of conditions closes.

sections.heading: 3.28 Why there is something
sections.why: It resolves the question of why anything exists by holding existing to be discovering itself, going on with no bottom.

sections.heading: 3.29 Bearer and bundle
sections.why: It resolves the substratum and bundle dispute as an object's presence being its properties' coupling.

sections.heading: 3.30 Laws of nature
sections.why: It resolves the governing and summarising accounts of laws as regularities arising with each coupling.

sections.heading: 3.31 Discrete and continuous
sections.why: It resolves the paradoxes of motion as one going on with a decomposition a frame imposes ahead of it.

sections.heading: 3.32 The felt and its describing
sections.why: It resolves the zombie and conceivability argument about consciousness as an interior reached only by coupling.

sections.heading: 3.33 Self and other
sections.why: Its dilemma as posed is evolutionary biology's dispute between kin and group selection accountings of fitness effects among social organisms, which is a biological subject.

sections.heading: 3.34 Purpose and mechanism
sections.why: It resolves the philosophical dispute over teleology and function as two observings of one living trait.

sections.heading: 3.35 Two observings at odds
sections.why: It resolves the epistemology of peer disagreement as a judging that the between of two selves makes case by case.

sections.heading: 3.36 Nature and convention
sections.why: It resolves the legal positivism and natural law dispute in philosophy of law as validity made with each applying.

sections.heading: 3.37 A listing, observing it from inward and from outward
sections.why: It resolves the Skolem paradox in philosophy of mathematics as each model making its own countings.

sections.heading: PART FOUR · CO-SEQUENCING
sections.why: The part describes language, story, music, dancing and living together as shared co-sequencing between selves, a subject of human social life rather than of philosophy's dilemmas.
sections.home: Exhibit_NINE_Natural_Human_Society_v391.md (Natural Human Society: Geodesic Method of Human Social Moral Co-Competencing)

sections.heading: 4.1 Human ways, parallel floating neutrals
sections.why: It describes human ways of making meaning together, such as language, music, dance and cohabiting, as two selves co-sequencing, which is human social life and not a philosophical dilemma.
sections.home: Exhibit_NINE_Natural_Human_Society_v391.md (Natural Human Society: Geodesic Method of Human Social Moral Co-Competencing)

sections.heading: 4.2 One form at many betweens
sections.why: It claims that human ways, the periodic table, the genetic code and networks are one form at many betweens, a subject of the one universal form rather than of philosophy.
sections.home: Natural_Intelligence_v391.md (Natural Intelligence: The Universal Method of Same-Existing)

sections.heading: PART FIVE · GATHERING
sections.why: The part is a register of philosophy's commonly known dilemmas, each listed with its coupling, register and fixing.

sections.heading: 5.1 Register, one binary and no grade
sections.why: It sets out the two registers and the fixing column used to account for every philosophical dilemma in the gathering.

sections.heading: 5.2 Metaphysics
sections.why: It lists the metaphysical dilemmas with the coupling each splits, its register and its fixing.

sections.heading: 5.3 Epistemology
sections.why: It lists the epistemological dilemmas with the coupling each splits, its register and its fixing.

sections.heading: 5.4 Mind
sections.why: It lists the dilemmas of philosophy of mind with the coupling each splits, its register and its fixing.

sections.heading: 5.5 Ethics
sections.why: It lists the ethical dilemmas with the coupling each splits, its register and its fixing.

sections.heading: 5.6 Aesthetics
sections.why: It lists the dilemmas of aesthetics with the coupling each splits, its register and its fixing.

sections.heading: 5.7 Language and logic
sections.why: It lists the dilemmas of philosophy of language, logic and mathematics with the coupling each splits, its register and its fixing.

sections.heading: 5.8 Religion and the political
sections.why: It lists the dilemmas of philosophy of religion and political philosophy with the coupling each splits, its register and its fixing.

sections.heading: PART SIX · COHERING
sections.why: The part states what the file's re-couplings hold, what stays open, and the one result that would break its explaining.

sections.heading: 6.1 Standings open at this file's own turn
sections.why: It names questions this file leaves open for its next turn, such as which side of each seam is sharing and whether a dilemma seats onto a number; its first paragraph on a self not experiencing its own competency leans toward another file's subject.

sections.heading: 6.2 Cohering, and the reaching
sections.why: It sums up the thirty-seven seams that hold, lists the dilemmas still reaching, and states the test that would break the method.

summary: Of 60 sections (6 parts and 54 numbered sections), 55 are within the title and subtitle and 5 are outside: 3.22 Structure and agency, 3.33 Self and other, and all of Part Four with 4.1 and 4.2. The file is mostly observing, since nearly every section takes a dilemma a tradition fixes and resolves it, with possibling where two selves share a between (3.6, 3.14, 3.35, Part Four) and discovering in the seam method (2.2) and the open standings (6.1). No section is a strict hole, but Part Four's language, story, music and dance rest only loosely in Natural Human Society because no title names the arts or culture, and the first paragraph of 6.1 on a self's own competency belongs more to another file than to philosophy.
